chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Performing among whites; black audience seating
summary: Outside Harlem he was the only black act before mostly white audiences without hassles; black patrons sat scattered in balconies.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But black entertainment, it was starting to develop in terms of on the stage a lot more certainly in the 20's and 30's more than it ever had been before.
Yes, but I wasn't in there.
You were performing mostly around whites at that time.
Yeah, mh-hm.
Except for when you went up to Harlem.
That's right.
Anywhere else around the country was all whites and you were the only black guys.
That's right.
Pretty much so.
That's right.
How did you feel being around all those white people?
All right, felt all right. I know I wouldn't be there unless I was doing something. I got to be doing something outstanding to be there, man.
How did they respond to you?
Great. Great, everything was great.
Never any hassles?
No, no hassles.
And I know that most of your audiences were white, too.
Yep.
Were there ever blacks in the audience?
Yeah, scattered. All scattered.
Or would they
No, they were scattered on the ground floor. First balcony and the ground floor, second balcony.
There weren't any next to the whites in the audience, were there?
Yeah.
Remember, we're talking about the 20's and 30's.
